verdict_text:
NO

The merge takes the second task vector against the already-modified base instead of the unmodified one. The script computes `tmp = base + 0.4*(ft1 - base)` and then `out = tmp + 0.4*(ft2 - tmp)`, which equals `base + 0.4*(ft1 - base) + 0.4*(ft2 - base) - 0.16*(ft1 - base)`. The spec's step 2 requires `out[X] = base[X] + lambda*(ft1[X] - base[X]) + lambda*(ft2[X] - base[X])`, with each difference taken against the unmodified base, and the "Why it is meaningful" section explicitly calls out this ordering hazard. The extra `-0.16*(ft1 - base)` term will exceed the 1e-5 relative Frobenius tolerance on all 48 merged tensors. The verification, unchanged-tensor handling, counts and output location are otherwise correct.
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
